sophia (runtime): heads-up — noticed tail latency bump in eu-west last 2 hours. P50 ok, p95 -> 300ms, p99 spikes to 1.6s and correlates with cross-zone spill events.
raj (infra): heap of spill logs? can you paste the spill reason?
sophia (runtime): minimal — scheduler elected cross-zone spill when local queue depth hit soft_limit. logs show `spill_reason: affinity_loss` then a kernel fallback: `selected_kernel: int8_fallback_slow` for a bunch of 128–256 token requests.
mike (platform): that kernel fallback sounds like quant kernel selection mismatch. did the model/seqLen histogram change?
elin (ml): checked recent traffic: larger fraction of short-chat requests (<=64 tokens) but with high concurrency bursts from an internal test — changes kernel pick heuristics. profiler shows hotpath time increased in `kv_cache.lookup` misses when spill occurs.
sophia (runtime): exact seqLen distribution: 60% <=64, 30% 65-256, 10% >256. When we spill to another zone, KV cache locality drops and miss rate goes from ~4% -> ~28%. That increases token generation latency and triggers slower kernel due to different batch packing shape.
natalie (sre): deploy-bot flagged higher error budget consumption; paging noise is starting. Can we short-circuit spill for shards with high KV affinity?
sophia (runtime): proposal: adjust continuous-batching heuristic — raise per-host token_budget_target for short-seq dominant workloads so local queue is more willing to form slightly larger batches instead of spilling. Also make cross-zone spill policy stricter: prefer local soft_reserve until kv_miss_rate > 15%.
raj (infra): risky — if we hold too long local, we could starve other tenants. need per-tenant token_budget caps and a fast fallback. can we tune by region only for eu-west workload tag?
el in (ml): small tweak: for short sequences we should bias kernel selection to `fast_small_seq` kernels even when batch shapes vary — microbenchmarks show `fast_small_seq` gives 20% lower latency for mixed padding.
mike (platform): ok concrete steps: 1) run an A/B where eu-west hosts get token_budget_target +25% for <=64 token requests, 2) change spill threshold to require kv_miss_rate > 0.15 and queue_age > 15ms, 3) add kernel-selection override flag for small-seq bias.
sophia (runtime): I can run a canary on 2 racks in eu-west tonight. quick perf check locally: pinned 64-token workload -> batch formation improved from avg 3 -> 4 requests per batch, latency down 90ms.
raj (infra): add metrics: `kv_cache.local_hit_ratio`, `batch_shape_entropy`, `kernel_fallbacks_per_min` to dashboards. If kernel_fallbacks_per_min > 5 for >5min revert.
elin (ml): also add a cheap profiler sample to record batch_shapes per kernel selection. a one-line change in profiler logging will surface alignment issues.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: eu-west-rack-2 @ 23:30 UTC. CI: green.
sophia (runtime): post-canary checklist: collect kv_hit_ratio, p95/p99, kernel_fallbacks, token throughput. If p99 improves and kv_hit_ratio >= 85% we rollout region-wide.
natalie (sre): ping me 10m before canary so we can watch alerts. I'll temporarily raise paging threshold by 10% for the canary window. :thumbsup:
sophia (runtime): thanks — will post quick log snippet after first 5m.
raj (infra): one more thought — long term we should encode per-shard KV affinity score into the scheduler so spill cost is estimated in ms rather than just queue depth. I'll open a follow-up ticket.
sophia (runtime): agreed. creating ticket now -> https://rwd.internal/tickets/INFR-9823
mike (platform): great. capture results in the perf runbook and we can bake safe defaults into the region profile.
sophia (runtime): ok launching canary in 10m, will report back.
